title: Layer-Resolved Topological Metals in the Bilayer Lieb Lattice
authors: Mengjie Yang, S Rahul, Giandomenico Palumbo
abstract: We identify a two-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological metallic phase on a bilayer Lieb lattice, characterized by a quantized layer--resolved pseudo-spin Chern number. Without the orbital-angular-momentum-dependent (OAM-dependent) coupling, the system gives rise to a time-reversal-invariant topological semimetal with a zero indirect gap and quantized pseudo-spin Chern number. Opposite-sign intralayer OAM-dependent coupling immediately converts the zero-indirect-gap semimetal into a metal, in which the global spectrum is metallic while the layer--resolved pseudo-spin Chern number remains well defined as long as the direct gap at each crystal momentum and the pseudo-spin gap remain open. The model also exhibits asymmetric boundary states: in the semimetallic regime, one edge hosts perfectly flat bands, whereas the opposite edge supports gapless counter-propagating modes forming a one-dimensional Dirac cone. An edge-localized interlayer coupling gaps only the counter-propagating edge states, leaving the flat-band edge essentially intact, while intralayer OAM-dependent coupling bends the exact flat band into a dispersive boundary mode without affecting the gapped Dirac edge. These results open a route toward the controlled engineering of layer--resolved topological gapless phases in synthetic and quantum materials.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates topological metallic phases on a bilayer Lieb lattice, utilizing a layer-resolved pseudo-spin Chern number as the key diagnostic tool. It demonstrates how tuning coupling strengths can drive the system from a semimetal to a metal while preserving quantized topology. The findings offer a blueprint for engineering controlled, gapless edge states in synthetic quantum materials.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize a two-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological metallic phase on a bilayer Lieb lattice, focusing on the quantization of layer-resolved pseudo-spin Chern number.
main_result: The system realizes a 'pseudo-spin Chern metal' where opposite-sign OAM coupling converts a semimetal into a metal while preserving quantized topology. The boundary states are asymmetric, featuring both flat bands and gapless Dirac cones.
method: Theoretical analysis using projected pseudo-spin spectra to calculate the layer-resolved pseudo-spin Chern number ($C_s$) and analyzing edge physics via continuum models.
model_or_system: The model is a bilayer Lieb lattice for spinless fermions, analyzed through Hamiltonians incorporating interlayer coupling ($t_\perp$) and intralayer Orbital-Angular-Momentum-dependent (OAM) couplings. The system exhibits distinct semimetallic and metallic regimes.
key_observables: Pseudo-spin Chern Number ($C_s$), direct gap ($\Delta_{	ext{dir}}$), indirect gap ($\Delta_{	ext{ind}}$), flat band existence, and Dirac cone formation at edges.
important_parameters: The strength of the OAM coupling (e.g., $\lambda_{SO}$ or $H_{SOC}$) which drives the semimetal-to-metal transition; maintaining open direct and pseudo-spin gaps.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining topological invariants using projected operators, assuming that the gap closing/opening dictates the phase transitions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate bulk spectra showing the semimetal-to-metal transition as a function of coupling strength, and diagrams detail the asymmetric nature of boundary states (flat bands vs. Dirac cones).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the topological semimetallic phase via $C_s$, then introducing OAM coupling to induce metallicity while maintaining quantized topology, and finally analyzing the distinct, asymmetric edge physics.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical framework for engineering topologically non-trivial gapless phases in synthetic systems by controlling layer-resolved pseudo-spin degrees of freedom. The concept of 'pseudo-spin' is highly relevant to AMO platforms using internal states.
